summary: Senegal is one of West Africa's easiest doors: ECOWAS citizens move freely, a broad list including the EU, UK, US, Canada, India, Japan and much of Africa enters visa-free for up to 90 days, and many remaining nationalities can obtain a visa on arrival at Dakar's airport for stays of about a month.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required when arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, and the vaccine is recommended for all travelers to Senegal. Carry your yellow card, especially on overland routes.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Senegal

travelInsurance.text: Not required for entry, but recommended — Dakar has reasonable private clinics, while care up-country is basic.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Senegal

onwardTicket.text: Visa-free and visa-on-arrival travelers should hold a return or onward ticket and proof of accommodation — both are standard conditions for the Dakar airport visa on arrival and are checked by airlines.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Senegal

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers may ask visitors to show means of support for their stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Senegal

currencyLimits.text: Large amounts of cash — above roughly the equivalent of XOF 1,000,000 in foreign currency — should be declared on arrival; confirm current thresholds with Senegalese customs before carrying large sums.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Senegal

notes: Drones require prior authorization from the Senegalese aviation authority — flying one without a permit risks confiscation.

payments.text: Cards work in Dakar's hotels, supermarkets and better restaurants, but mobile money (Wave, Orange Money) and cash rule everywhere else. Keep small XOF notes for taxis, markets and up-country travel.

safety.text: Senegal is one of West Africa's most stable democracies and most visits are trouble-free. Watch for pickpocketing and bag-snatching on Dakar's corniche and in markets, and take advice before traveling to parts of the Casamance near the Gambia and Guinea-Bissau borders, where residual caution applies off the main routes.

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March is dry and relatively cool — best for Dakar, the Sine-Saloum delta and Saint-Louis; the rains run roughly July to September.

tips.text: The visa on arrival is issued at Dakar's Blaise Diagne Airport only — not at land or sea borders. If you're arriving overland and are not visa-exempt, get an embassy visa first.
Carry your yellow fever certificate — it's demanded when you arrive from a risk country, which includes most overland routes into Senegal.

In the Casamance, stick to main roads and daylight travel near the Gambian and Bissau-Guinean borders — isolated banditry and legacy landmines persist off the beaten track, though Cap Skirring and Ziguinchor are visited routinely.
Wave and Orange Money are how Senegal pays — even fruit stalls take them. A local SIM plus a mobile-money wallet saves endless small-cash hassles.
Around Dakar's sights, polite-but-firm refusals handle persistent touts and "guides"; agree taxi fares before getting in, as meters are not used.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Senegal?
faq.answer: Many travelers don't. ECOWAS citizens enter freely, and passport holders from the EU, UK, US, Canada, India, Japan and a broad list of African and other states get 90 visa-free days. Many other nationalities can obtain a visa on arrival at Dakar airport for about a month, while the rest apply at a Senegalese embassy.

faq.question: How long can US and EU citizens stay in Senegal?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days visa-free. For longer stays, apply for an extension or a long-stay visa through the Senegalese authorities before your 90 days run out.

faq.question: How does Senegal's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities (including most African Union states and countries such as Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Israel, Türkiye, Thailand and Russia) can be issued a visa on landing at Blaise Diagne International Airport for a stay of up to one month. It is not available at land borders, and you should carry a return ticket and proof of accommodation.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Senegal?
faq.answer: A certificate is mandatory only if you arrive from a country with yellow fever risk, but that covers most of Senegal's neighbors, and the vaccine is recommended for all visitors, so carry your yellow card.

faq.question: Is Senegal safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Broadly yes — it's among West Africa's most stable countries and the tourist circuit (Dakar, Saly, Saint-Louis, Sine-Saloum) is well traveled. The main annoyances are petty theft and scams in Dakar; parts of the Casamance borderlands call for extra care.
